count_records.description: Count an object's records, all of them or those matching a rule. Uses one API call.
count_records.name: count_records

parameters.description: The Knack object (table), such as object_1.
parameters.name: object_key

parameters.description: The field to filter on.
parameters.name: field_key

parameters.description: How to compare. Blank checks, 'is any' and the 'today' / 'current time' operators need no value.
parameters.name: operator

parameters.description: The value to compare with. To match a connected record, use the connection field with 'is' and the connected record's id. Dates use the field's own format, such as 09/24/2026.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: For 'is during the previous/next', 'is before the previous' and 'is after the next': how many units, such as 3.
parameters.name: range_amount

parameters.description: For the 'is during ...' operators: the unit, such as days, weeks, months or years.
parameters.name: range_unit

parameters.description: Optional extra rules in Knack's filter format, such as {"match": "or", "rules": [{"field": "field_1", "operator": "contains", "value": "Ltd"}]}. Combined with the rule above.
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Whether records must match all rules or any rule.
parameters.name: match

create_record.description: Create a record in an object. Fields left out get their default value. Form record rules do not run.
create_record.display_str_template: Create a record in Knack object {0}
create_record.name: create_record

parameters.description: The Knack object (table), such as object_1.
parameters.name: object_key

parameters.description: The new record's values. Fill in the fields to set and leave the rest blank. Name, Address, Email and Link values take JSON such as {"first": "Ada", "last": "Lovelace"}; a connection takes a list of record ids; a file or image field takes the id from 'Upload a file'; Yes/No takes true, false or kn-blank to clear it.
parameters.name: fields

returns.description: A Knack record. Besides id it carries one key per field, such as field_1 (and field_1_raw when the format is 'both').
